notes: PSA 7 ng/mL. PI-RADS 5. PSAD 0.12. Prostate volume 60 mL. csPCa 0.85.

note_sections.t: Current PSA elevation and previous biopsy outcomes warrant clinical reassessment.

A 55-year-old male initially investigated for a late 2022 PSA elevation underwent a diagnostic biopsy that established ISUP Group 3 disease. Hypertension remains managed with amlodipine, lisinopril, and metoprolol, with cardiology tracking showing stable parameters. A retired bank clerk, he resides alone despite being married; his spouse acts as his main contact and attends clinic visits. He keeps a BMI of 30.1, quit smoking in 2016 after a 34 pack-year habit, and jogs 5 km three times weekly. Lower urinary tract symptoms score 8/35 on the IPSS, remaining mild without catheterisation or TURP history. Podiatry visits maintain stable foot care, while six physiotherapy sessions addressed chronic lower back pain. Large-print correspondence is requested to accommodate visual impairment.
DRE: Prostate appears symmetrically enlarged, smooth to palpation, lacking nodules or asymmetry. General assessment shows stable vitals (BP 119/78 mmHg, HR 70 bpm) and a soft, non-tender abdomen.
